title: Lighthouse Infer - developer activation & pricing sketches
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact working brief for a developer-first hosted-API activation flow and accompanying pricing language. Goal: reduce time-to-first-successful-inference, make economic tradeoffs explicit, and test simple copy that resonates with engineers who value speed, debuggability, and predictable costs.

Quick thesis (one line):
Engineers choose Redwood Hosted when they can go from code to meaningful inference in minutes, understand cost per request, and have clear escape hatches (local/private deployment) when they need it. Messaging should therefore signal speed, observability, and predictable unit economics.

Target developer persona snippets:
- Prototype engineer at a seed-stage startup: wants a single API call to ship an MVP; cares about latency and cost but prioritizes shipping fast.
- Platform engineer at a mid-market SaaS: needs predictable bills and per-route observability; likely to evaluate Dedicated/Private for isolation.
- ML engineer validating a model: cares about token-level profiles, batch vs stream performance, and reproducible rollouts.

Core value props (developer framing):
- Integrate in under 5 minutes: SDK + one-line curl examples that return a meaningful output within the first call.
- Debuggable responses: request id + trace URL returned on error; replayable prompt + deterministic seed for evals.
- Transparent unit economics: per-token and per-embedding cost shown inline in console + sample cost calc.
- Predictable performance: default SLOs for cold/hot start latency and an easy path to reserved capacity.
- Safe fallbacks: automatic model variant fallback when capacity constrained, with explicit cost/latency tradeoff.

Quickstart angles (three short flows to A/B test):
1) 60-second Hello World (low friction):
   - Copy/paste curl that returns a short completion and a cost estimate.
   - CTA: "Try it now with free credits"
   - KPI: time-to-first-successful-request, activation rate within 1 hour.

2) App stitch (30-min integration):
   - Example: embed text generation into a tiny web form + streaming.
   - Include sample SDK snippet, suggested batch settings for latency vs cost, and console dashboard link.
   - KPI: percent of users who hit first 1000 tokens within 72 hours.

3) Eval-to-rollout (proof-of-quality path, 1–2 days):
   - Guided flow: run prompt set -> record outputs -> baseline quality metric -> canary rollout with automatic fallback.
   - KPI: time from prompt-set upload to canary deploy.

Pricing language drafts (framing + microcopy to test):
- Primary framing: "Pay-as-you-go. Clear per-token math, predictable monthly caps."
- Short explainer (console microcopy): "Estimated cost is based on tokens generated and tokens in request. Use the estimator to preview monthly spend."
- Starter credits blurb: "Free credits to experiment — keep your billing details private until you hit production."
- Reserved path: "Reserve capacity for predictable throughput and lower unit costs. Start with a monthly commitment and scale without surprises."
- Pricing experiment variants to A/B test (microcopy):
   A: "Tokens only: pay per request. No hidden compute fees."
   B: "Predictable tiers: flat per-100k-token buckets + overage priced transparently."
   C: "Engineer-first: hourly reserved pools for teams that need consistent latency."

Competitive note (quick scan for positioning):
- Competitors emphasize access to models or low sticker price per token. Our differentiation should not be "cheaper" as primary claim; lead with developer productivity (time-to-first-successful-inference), observability, and deployment escape routes (Dedicated/Private).
- Callouts to include in materials: "show sample latency graphs vs synthetic cost curves" and "compare ease-of-rollback and per-request tracing."

Sample onboarding microcopy and UX snippets (to put in flow or emails):
- Welcome email subject: "Your Redwood keys: 10 minutes to first inference"
- Console header: "Run your first request — sample prompt included"
- Inline cost tip: "This request ~ 12 tokens = ~$0.00X. Est. 10k requests/month = $Y."
- Error state CTA: "View trace for this request or fallback to a lower-cost model"

Operational hooks (what engineering needs to expose):
- Request id and trace link on every response (success + error).
- Token-level cost return value for sample requests in console.
- Playground link that exposes batching and streaming toggles.

Measurement plan (metrics to instrument pre-launch):
- Activation: percent of signups that complete first successful request within 1 hour.
- Time to first deploy: median time from signup to first production route (days).
- Cost comprehension: percent of users who view the estimator before issuing >1k tokens.
- Retention: 30-day DAU for users who used quickstart vs those who didn’t.

A/B test ideas (prioritized):
- Test call-to-action language on signup: "Start in 60s" vs "Try with free credits" (measure activation).
- Test pricing copy: per-token math visible upfront vs only in billing docs (measure trial-to-paid conversion).
- Test default SDK examples: minimal vs annotated (measure time-to-first-success).

Messaging dos and don’ts: quick guide
- Do: show example output on landing pages — engineers want to see real responses.
- Do: surface latency and cost numbers early.
- Don't: bury operational caveats (limits, cold-starts) behind legal docs. Engineers will find them; better to surface with tradeoffs.

Next steps / action items (owners and rough timeline):
- Wire a new 60s-hello-world flow in console (Maya) — prototype by 2025-02-05.
- Add token-estimator snippet and inline sample costs (Product) — 2025-02-12.
- Draft 3 pricing microcopy variants and set up randomized experiment in signup funnel (GTM) — 2025-02-18.
- Instrument activation + cost-comprehension metrics in analytics (Eng/data) — 2025-02-20.

Open questions / things to validate:
- What baseline free-credit amount meaningfully increases time-to-first-success without inflating our trial burn? (finance input needed)
- Will per-request cost visibility cause sticker shock or increase trust? (research via small user interviews)
- How to succinctly describe model fallback behavior in one line without confusing developers?

Appendix: example minimal quickstart (for copy into console)
- curl example (single call):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"Summarize: "Redwood is..."","max_tokens":60}'

  Response fields to show in console: request_id, elapsed_ms, cost_estimate_tokens, trace_url.

End of brief.

Notes: keep this doc living; it should be the single source for the quickstart copy experiment until we pick a winner.
